title: The Ant and the Grasshopper
source: Aesop's Fables (public domain), gently retold for bedtime

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Once upon a time, on a warm summer day, the meadow was golden and full of sunshine.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: High on a tall stalk of grass, a grasshopper sat with his little fiddle, playing a happy tune.

lines.speaker: grasshopper
lines.speech: [cheerful, singing a little] La la la... What a beautiful day! The sun is shining, and there is nothing in the world to do but sing!
lines.text: La la la... What a beautiful day! The sun is shining, and there is nothing in the world to do but sing!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Down below, a little ant came marching past, carrying a big grain of wheat on her back.

lines.speaker: grasshopper
lines.speech: [friendly, curious] Hello, little Ant! Why are you working so hard on such a lovely day? Come and sing with me!
lines.text: Hello, little Ant! Why are you working so hard on such a lovely day? Come and sing with me!

lines.speaker: ant
lines.speech: [kindly, a little out of breath] Thank you, Grasshopper, but I can't. I'm gathering food for the winter. When the cold comes, there will be nothing left to eat.
lines.text: Thank you, Grasshopper, but I can't. I'm gathering food for the winter. When the cold comes, there will be nothing left to eat.

lines.speaker: ant
lines.text: You should gather some too.

lines.speaker: grasshopper
lines.speech: [laughs, carefree] Winter? Oh, winter is so far away! There's plenty of food today. Why worry about tomorrow?
lines.text: Winter? Oh, winter is so far away! There's plenty of food today. Why worry about tomorrow?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So the grasshopper went on singing, and the ant went on working.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: All summer long, she carried seeds and grains, one at a time, down into her cosy little home under the ground.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And all summer long, the grasshopper played his fiddle, and danced in the sun.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then, the days grew shorter. The leaves turned red and gold, and they began to fall, one by one.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The wind grew cooler, and the meadow grew quiet. But the grasshopper still didn't gather any food.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And then, one morning, the meadow was white. Soft snow had fallen everywhere, covering the grass and the flowers.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The grasshopper looked for something to eat. But there was nothing. Not a single seed. Not a single leaf.

lines.speaker: grasshopper
lines.speech: [shivering, sad] Brrr... I'm so cold... and so hungry. Oh, what am I going to do?
lines.text: Brrr... I'm so cold... and so hungry. Oh, what am I going to do?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then he remembered the little ant. So he hopped through the snow, slowly, slowly, until he found her tiny door.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Knock, knock, knock.

lines.speaker: ant
lines.speech: [surprised, then warm] Why, Grasshopper! You're shivering! Come in, come in, out of the cold.
lines.text: Why, Grasshopper! You're shivering! Come in, come in, out of the cold.

lines.speaker: grasshopper
lines.speech: [sheepish, quietly] I'm sorry, Ant. You were right. I sang all summer, and I didn't save anything for the winter.
lines.text: I'm sorry, Ant. You were right. I sang all summer, and I didn't save anything for the winter.

lines.speaker: ant
lines.speech: [kindly] That's alright. I have plenty to share. Here, have some warm seed soup.
lines.text: That's alright. I have plenty to share. Here, have some warm seed soup.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The grasshopper ate, and ate, until his tummy was full and his toes were warm.

lines.speaker: grasshopper
lines.speech: [grateful, touched] Thank you, Ant. Next summer, I will work with you. And maybe... in the evenings, I can play you a song?
lines.text: Thank you, Ant. Next summer, I will work with you. And maybe... in the evenings, I can play you a song?

lines.speaker: ant
lines.speech: [happy, smiling] I would like that very much.
lines.text: I would like that very much.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So, all winter long, the two friends stayed warm and cosy together. And every evening, the grasshopper played a soft, sleepy song.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Because it is good to play, and it is good to sing. But it is also good to work hard, and to get ready for what's to come.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Outside, the snow fell softly. Inside, the little ones were fast asleep.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Goodnight, little one. Sweet dreams.
